clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country to Sorrel Valley in March 1952: within months, June grew homesick and wrote to her sister daily, Walter stayed out in the orchard from dark to dark, Glen got into fights at school and was sent home twice, Walter cut off his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter and June rowed over money for new trees, and by September 1953 June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. These shifts pile up over a year and a half in the new place, each touching on the strain of the move and the family's settling into it.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: within months, Walter drank heavily most nights, he and Glen blamed each other for the loan, Glen took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, you began wetting the bed in April 1969, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working, and by October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees. The shifts reach across autumn and winter into spring, touching Walter's trouble, Glen's overfunctioning under the strain, and the children's symptoms as the family reacted to the loss of the orchard.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: within months, Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours, he and Marian had loud fights at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and said little to your mother, your grandfather Walter drank again after six years off it, and by June 1976 you were eating again and made the track team. The shifts touch Glen's fall in functioning, the couple's conflict, Marian's overfunctioning, your own symptoms and distance from her, and Walter's relapse nearby in the family.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma, Hollis's mother, selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: within months, you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice, Wilma took over Lily's care, you broke out in eczema on both hands, you and Hollis had rows most nights, and by June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town, and over the summer your eczema cleared. The shifts reach from spring through autumn, touching your conflict with Wilma, Hollis's alignment with his mother, the children's disturbance, and your own physical response to the strain of the household.
